criteria.long_description: The ZIP contains PDF rules, PDF printable components, and labelled simulations or facsimiles for required non-printable pieces; the inventory and supplied materials allow reconstruction of the game.

ratings.description: Strong: the package is complete, internally consistent, and ready to reconstruct
Partial: the game is substantially reconstructable but a limited component, file, or consistency problem interferes
Not demonstrated: missing core materials prevent an assessable playable reconstruction

criteria.long_description: The rules state audience, player count, duration, goal, inventory, setup, sequence, legal actions, resolutions, end condition, and tie handling, with examples or diagrams where needed; unfamiliar players can proceed with little or no designer intervention.

ratings.description: Strong: the rules support accurate independent play and resolve likely questions
Partial: play can proceed but recurring ambiguities or omissions require interpretation
Not demonstrated: the rules do not support independent play

criteria.long_description: Players encounter viable consequential choices, receive legible feedback, and can connect actions to changes in state; rules and components interact in support of the stated audience and experience goal.

ratings.description: Strong: meaningful choices, feedback, and rule interactions form a coherent playable system
Partial: a system is playable but choices, feedback, or interactions are thin, disconnected, or inconsistent
Not demonstrated: no assessable coherent system or consequential choice

criteria.long_description: Blind or low-intervention testing records observable evidence such as duration, questions, strategies, stalls, and outcome ranges; the team uses that evidence to revise or retain features so intended choices remain meaningfully viable.

ratings.description: Strong: relevant evidence and before/after reasoning support convincing balance and revision decisions
Partial: testing occurred but evidence, balance reasoning, follow-up, or revision is thin
Not demonstrated: no assessable test, balance, and revision record

criteria.long_description: The video demonstrates setup, representative play, consequential choices, feedback, and an end or scoring procedure; materials are readable and usable, and third-party work is accurately credited and licensed.

ratings.description: Strong: gameplay is clearly evidenced, materials support access, and credits/licences are complete
Partial: the evidence remains assessable but a limited video, access, credit, or licence problem interferes
Not demonstrated: gameplay evidence is absent or serious access/credit problems remain

criteria.description: Individual contribution, analysis, and applicable AI appendix
criteria.long_description: Each student identifies concrete contributions and analyzes one effect on rules, experience, testing, or production. When AI contributed to submitted work, complete relevant chatlogs are included without credentials or private third-party information.

ratings.description: Strong: every contribution entry is specific and analytical, and any applicable appendix is complete
Partial: entries or analysis are uneven, or an applicable appendix has a limited omission
Not demonstrated: contribution evidence or analysis is absent, or an applicable appendix has a material omission
